chapter.li: LEChapter1 Verse1 James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad: Greeting. VerseEnd

Verse2 My brethren, count it all joy when you fall into many afflictions, VerseEnd Verse3 knowing this, that the trying of your faith works patience; VerseEnd Verse4 but let patience have its perfect work, that you may be perfect and entire, lacking nothing. VerseEnd Verse5 If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all liberally and upbraids not, and it shall be given him. VerseEnd Verse6 But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering, for he that wavers is like a wave of the sea, driven with the wind and tossed; VerseEnd Verse7 for let not that man think that he shall receive anything of the Lord. VerseEnd Verse8 A double-minded man is unstable in all his ways. VerseEnd

Verse9 Let the brother of low degree rejoice in that he is exalted, VerseEnd Verse10 but the rich in that he is made low, because as the flower of the grass, he shall pass away. VerseEnd Verse11 For the sun is no sooner risen with a burning heat but it withers the grass, and the flower thereof falls, and the grace of the fashion of it perishes. So also shall the rich man fade away in his ways. VerseEnd

Verse12 Blessed is the man that resists temptation, for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life which the Lord has promised to them that love him. VerseEnd Verse13 Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God. For God cannot be tempted with evil, neither tempts he any man, VerseEnd Verse14 but every man is tempted when he is drawn away of his own lust and enticed. VerseEnd Verse15 Then, when lust has conceived, it brings forth sin; and sin, when it is finished, brings forth death. VerseEnd Verse16 Do not err, my beloved brethren. VerseEnd

Verse17 Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above and comes down from the Father of Lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning. VerseEnd Verse18 Of his own will, he begot us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures. VerseEnd Verse19 Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath VerseEnd — Verse20 for the wrath of man works not the righteousness of God. VerseEnd

Verse21 Wherefore, lay aside all filthiness and excess of wickedness, and receive with meekness the grafted word, which is able to save your souls. VerseEnd Verse22 But be doers of the word and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves, VerseEnd Verse23 for if any are a hearer of the word and not a doer, he is like unto a man beholding his natural face in a mirror, VerseEnd Verse24 for he beholds himself and goes his way, and immediately forgets what manner of man he was. VerseEnd Verse25 But whoever looks into the perfect law of liberty and continues therein, he being not a forgetful hearer but a doer of the work, this man shall be blessed in his deed. VerseEnd

Verse26 If any man among you seem to be religious and bridles not his tongue, but deceives his own heart, this man’s religion is vain. VerseEnd Verse27 Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this: to visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the vices of the world. VerseEnd

LEChapter2 Verse1 My brethren, you cannot have the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, and yet have respect to persons. VerseEnd Verse2 Now if there come unto your assembly a man with a gold ring, in fine apparel, and there come in also a poor man in vile raiment, VerseEnd Verse3 and you have respect to him that wears the fine clothing and say unto him, Sit here in a good place, and say to the poor, Stand there, or sit here under my footstool, VerseEnd Verse4 are you not then in yourselves partial judges? And become evil in your thoughts? VerseEnd

Verse5 Listen, my beloved brethren. Has not God chosen the poor of this world, rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom which he has promised to them that love him? VerseEnd Verse6 But you have despised the poor. Do not rich men oppress you and draw you before the judgment seats? VerseEnd Verse7 Do they not blaspheme that worthy name by which you are called? VerseEnd

Verse8 If you fulfill the royal law according to the scripture — You shall love your neighbor as yourself — you do well. VerseEnd Verse9 But if you have respect to persons, you commit sin and are convicted of the law as transgressors; VerseEnd Verse10 for whoever shall, save in one point, keep the whole law, he is guilty of all. VerseEnd Verse11 For he that said, Do not commit adultery, said also, Do not kill. Now if you commit no adultery, yet if you kill, you have become a transgressor of the law. VerseEnd Verse12 So speak and so do as they that shall be judged by the law of liberty, VerseEnd Verse13 for he shall have judgment without mercy who has shown no mercy, and mercy rejoices against judgment. VerseEnd

Verse14 What profit is it, my brethren, for a man to say he has faith, and has not works? Can faith save him? VerseEnd Verse15 Yea, a man may say, I will show you I have faith without works. But I say, show me your faith without works and I will show you my faith by my works. For if a brother or sister are naked and destitute, VerseEnd Verse16 and one of you say, Depart in peace, be warmed and filled — notwithstanding he give not those things which are needful to the body — what profit is your faith unto such? VerseEnd Verse17 Even so faith, if it has not works, it is dead, being alone. VerseEnd Verse18 Therefore will you know, O vain man, that faith without works is dead and cannot save you. VerseEnd

Verse19 You believe there is one God. You do well. The devils also believe and tremble. VerseEnd Verse20 You have made yourself like unto them, not being justified. VerseEnd Verse21 Was not Abraham, our father, justified by works when he had offered Isaac, his son, upon the altar? VerseEnd Verse22 Do you see how works wrought with his faith, and by works was faith made perfect? VerseEnd Verse23 And the scripture was fulfilled which says, Abraham believed God and it was imputed unto him for righteousness, and he was called the friend of God. VerseEnd Verse24 You see then that by works a man is justified, and not by faith only. VerseEnd Verse25 Likewise also, Rahab the harlot was justified by works when she had received the messengers and sent them out another way. VerseEnd Verse26 For as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead. VerseEnd

LEChapter3 Verse1 My brethren, strive not for the mastery, knowing that in so doing we shall receive the greater condemnation; VerseEnd Verse2 for in many things we offend all. If any man offend not in word, the same is a perfect man and able also to bridle the whole body. VerseEnd Verse3 Behold, we put bits in the horses’ mouths that they may obey us, and we turn about their whole body. VerseEnd Verse4 Behold also the ships, which though they are so great and are driven of fierce winds, yet are they turned about with a very small helm, wherever the helmsman desires. VerseEnd Verse5 Even so the tongue is a little member and boasts great things. Behold, how great a forest a little fire kindles; VerseEnd Verse6 and the tongue is a fire, a world of iniquity. So is the tongue among our members — that it defiles the whole body and sets on fire the course of nature; and it is set on fire of hell. VerseEnd Verse7 For every kind of beast, and of bird, and of serpent, and of things in the sea, is tamed and has been tamed of mankind; VerseEnd Verse8 but the tongue can no man tame. It is an unruly evil, full of deadly poison. VerseEnd Verse9 With it we bless God, even the Father; and with it we curse men, who are made after the similitude of God. VerseEnd Verse10 Out of the same mouth proceeds blessing and cursing. My brethren, these things ought not so to be. VerseEnd Verse11 Does a fountain send forth at the same place sweet water and bitter? VerseEnd Verse12 Can the fig tree, my brethren, bear olive berries? Either a vine, figs? So can no fountain both yield saltwater and fresh. VerseEnd

Verse13 Who is a wise man, and endowed with knowledge, among you? Let him show out of good conduct his works with meekness of wisdom. VerseEnd Verse14 But if you have bitter envying and strife in your hearts, glory not and lie not against the truth. VerseEnd Verse15 This wisdom descends not from above, but is earthly, sensual, devilish; VerseEnd Verse16 for where envying and strife are, there are confusion and every evil work. VerseEnd Verse17 But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, and easy to be entreated, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, and without hypocrisy. VerseEnd Verse18 And the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace, of them that make peace. VerseEnd

LEChapter4 Verse1 From where do wars and fightings come among you? Do they not come from here — even of your lusts that war in your members? VerseEnd Verse2 You lust, and have not. You kill, and desire to have, and cannot obtain. You fight and war, yet you have not, because you ask not. VerseEnd Verse3 You ask and receive not because you ask amiss, that you may consume it upon your lusts. VerseEnd

Verse4 You adulterers and adulteresses, do you not know that the friendship of the world is enmity with God? Whoever therefore will be a friend of the world is the enemy of God. VerseEnd Verse5 Do you think that the scripture says in vain, The spirit that dwells in us lusts to envy? VerseEnd Verse6 But he gives more grace. Wherefore, he says: God resists the proud, but gives grace unto the humble. VerseEnd Verse7 Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil and he will flee from you. VerseEnd Verse8 Draw near to God and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners, and purify your hearts, you double-minded. VerseEnd Verse9 Be afflicted, and mourn, and weep. Let your laughter be turned to mourning, and your joy to heaviness. VerseEnd Verse10 Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord and he shall lift you up. VerseEnd

Verse11 Speak not evil one of another, brethren. He that speaks evil of his brother and judges his brother speaks evil of the law and judges the law. But if you judge the law, you are not a doer of the law, but a judge. VerseEnd Verse12 There is one lawgiver, who is able to save and to destroy. Who are you that judges another? VerseEnd

Verse13 Come now, you that say, Today or tomorrow we will go into such a city, and continue there a year, and buy and sell, and get gain VerseEnd — Verse14 whereas you know not what shall be on the next day. For what is your life? It is even a vapor that appears for a little time and then vanishes away. VerseEnd Verse15 You ought to say, If the Lord wishes, we shall live and do this or that. VerseEnd Verse16 But now you rejoice in your boastings; all such rejoicing is evil. VerseEnd Verse17 Therefore, to him that knows to do good and does it not, to him it is sin. VerseEnd

LEChapter5 Verse1 Come now, you rich men, weep and howl for your miseries that shall come upon you. VerseEnd Verse2 Your riches are corrupted and your garments are moth-eaten. VerseEnd Verse3 Your gold and silver is cankered, and the rust of them shall be a witness against you, and shall eat your flesh like fire. You have heaped treasure together for the last days. VerseEnd Verse4 Behold, the hire of the laborers who have reaped down your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, cries, and the cries of them who have reaped are entered into the ears of the Lord of Hosts. VerseEnd Verse5 You have lived in pleasure on the earth and been wanton. You have nourished your hearts as in a day of slaughter. VerseEnd Verse6 You have condemned and killed the just, and he does not resist you. VerseEnd

Verse7 Be patient therefore, brethren, unto the coming of the Lord. Behold, the husbandman waits for the precious fruit of the earth and has long patience for it, until he receives the autumn and spring rain. VerseEnd Verse8 Be also patient; establish your hearts, for the coming of the Lord draws near. VerseEnd Verse9 Grudge not one against another, brethren, lest you should be condemned. Behold, the judge stands before the door. VerseEnd

Verse10 Take, my brethren, the prophets, who have spoken in the name of the Lord, for an example of suffering affliction and of patience. VerseEnd Verse11 Behold, we count them happy who endure. You have heard of the patience of Job, and have seen the end of the Lord, that the Lord is full of pity and of tender mercy. VerseEnd

Verse12 But above all things, my brethren, swear not — neither by Heaven, neither by the earth, neither by any other oath — but let your yea be yea, and your nay, nay, lest you fall into condemnation. VerseEnd

Verse13 Is any among you afflicted? Let him pray. Is any merry? Let him sing psalms. VerseEnd Verse14 Is any sick among you? Let him call for the elders of the church, and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord. VerseEnd Verse15 And the prayer of faith shall save the sick, and the Lord shall raise him up. And if he has committed sins, they shall be forgiven him. VerseEnd

Verse16 Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that you may be healed. The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man avails much. VerseEnd Verse17 Elijah was a man subject to like passions as we are, and he prayed earnestly that it might not rain, and it rained not on the earth for the space of three years and six months. VerseEnd Verse18 And he prayed again, and the heaven gave rain, and the earth brought forth her fruit. VerseEnd

Verse19 Brethren, if any of you do err from the truth and one convert him, VerseEnd Verse20 let him know that he who converts the sinner from the error of his way shall save a soul from death, and shall hide a multitude of sins. VerseEnd
